nodes.name: Amorphous NiMoOx co-precipitation
nodes.procedure: 20 ml of aqueous NiCl2·6H2O solution with a concentration of 1 M was prepared, denoted as solution A. 20 ml of aqueous Na2MoO4 solution with a concentration of 1 M was also prepared, denoted as solution B. Then, solution B was rapidly added to solution A under ultrasonic conditions at room temperature. Precipitates were formed immediately. After 10 min of ultrasonic vibration, the precipitates were collected by centrifugation and washed with water and ethanol three times.

nodes.name: Amorphous RuNiMoOx co-precipitation
nodes.procedure: 20 ml of aqueous NiCl2·6H2O solution with a concentration of 1 M was prepared, denoted as solution A. 20 ml of aqueous Na2MoO4 solution with a concentration of 1 M and containing RuCl3 was also prepared, denoted as solution B. The mass fraction of RuCl3 in solution B were 1 at.%, 2.5 at.%, and 5 at.%. Then, solution B was rapidly added to solution A under ultrasonic conditions at room temperature. Precipitates were formed immediately. After 10 min of ultrasonic vibration, the precipitates were collected by centrifugation and washed with water and ethanol three times.

nodes.name: Crystalline NiMoOx hydrothermal synthesis
nodes.procedure: 0.349 g Ni(NO3)2·6H2O and 0.371 g (NH4)6Mo7O24·4H2O were dissolved in 30 ml DI water and mixed under stirring for 30 min. Next, ammonium hydroxide was used to adjust pH = 7.0. The mixture was transferred into a Teflon-lined stainless-steel autoclave for hydrothermal treatment at 150 °C for 6 h. The precipitate was separated by centrifugation, washed with water and ethanol, and dried at 70 °C. The above products were annealed in air at 450 °C for 3 h, and the c-NMO was obtained.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD pattern of a-RNMO and a-NMO showed absence of crystalline phase, distinct from crystalline c-NMO with strong characteristic peaks.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The X-ray diffraction (XRD) pattern (Fig. 1b) showed the absence of a crystalline phase in a-NMO and a-RNMO, which was distinct from crystalline NiMoO4 (c-NMO) with strong characteristic peaks.

properties.peaks: Multiple sharp peaks indicating crystalline structure

nodes.characterization_summary: PDF analysis showed a-RNMO and a-NMO have long-range disordered but short-range ordered crystal structures with short-range correlation of about 9 Å; M–O and M–M bond lengths longer than c-NMO.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Fig. 1c-e, it was evident that for the pristine a-NMO and a-RNMO, the crystal structures were long-range disordered but short-range ordered... This analysis indicated that the amorphous structure had a short-range correlation of about 9 Å.

nodes.characterization_summary: HR-TEM image of a-RNMO showed no lattice fringes, combined with absence of diffraction rings in SAED pattern, indicating typical amorphous oxide formation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HR-TEM) image in Supplementary Fig. 2b-c showed no lattice fringes, combined with the absence of diffraction rings in the selected area electron diffraction (SAED) pattern (Supplementary Fig. 2d), together indicating typical amorphous oxide formation.

nodes.characterization_summary: AC-HAADF-STEM image showed monodispersed Ru single atoms (bright dots) in a-RNMO with isolated dispersion and no obvious atomic lattice distribution.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The presence of monodispersed Ru single atoms (bright dots marked by red circles in Fig. 1f) was observed by high-magnification aberration-corrected high-angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscopy (AC-HAADF-STEM) image.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS mapping revealed homogeneous spatial distribution of Ru, Ni, Mo, and O in a-RNMO.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Moreover, energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) mapping (Fig. 1h) revealed homogeneous spatial distribution of Ru, Ni, Mo, and O.

properties.description: Four-panel elemental distribution map with 200 nm scale bar

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-OES confirmed Ru content in a-RNMO was 2.28 at.% with Ru:Ni molar ratio ≈0.15.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The elemental composition of a‑RNMO was analyzed by inductively coupled plasma-optical emission spectroscopy (ICP‑OES) (Supplementary Table 2)... confirming the Ru content was 2.28 at.%.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni 2p XPS shows Ni2+ (78%) and Ni3+ species with lower binding energy shift in a-RNMO vs a-NMO (69% Ni2+); Mo 3d corresponds to Mo6+ unaffected by Ru; Ru 3p indicates Ru3.60+ valence.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Fig. 2a, the two main Ni 2p peaks of both a-NMO and a-RNMO were deconvoluted into Ni2+ (about 855 eV and 873 eV) and Ni3+ (about 857 eV and 875 eV) species, respectively. The incorporation of Ru resulted in an increased proportion of Ni2+ and a peak shift towards lower binding energy. Specifically, the percentage of Ni2+ species increased from 69% in a-NMO to 78% in a-RNMO... As for the Mo 3d spectra in Fig. 2b, the peaks corresponded to the Mo6+ signal. The valence state of Ru in a-RNMO, as shown in Fig. 2c, was approximately Ru3.60+.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni K-edge XANES showed slight decrease in Ni valence state by Ru introduction; Mo K-edge similar for a-NMO and a-RNMO indicating Mo6+; Ru K-edge negatively shifted vs RuO2 implying lower valence than Ru4+.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As observed in Fig. 2d, the normalized Ni K-edge XANES spectra showed a slight decrease in the valence state of Ni species by the introduction of Ru... For the K-edge of Ru (Fig. 2f), the edge position in a-RNMO was negatively shifted compared to RuO2, implying a slightly lower valence state than Ru4+.

nodes.characterization_summary: EXAFS showed reduced structural order in amorphous structures vs c-NMO; Ni-O at 1.59 Å, Mo-O at 1.32-1.35 Å longer than crystalline; Ru K-edge showed Ru-O at ~1.44 Å and second peak at ~2.76 Å indicating no Ru clusters.
nodes.evidence_snippet: FT analysis of a‑RNMO and a‑NMO revealed reduced structural order compared to c‑NMO... The first coordination shell corresponded to Ni-O bonds (~1.59 Å) in the amorphous structure... The Ru K‑edge EXAFS spectra (Fig. 2i) of a‑RNMO showed two notable peaks in R‑space.

nodes.characterization_summary: EIS Nyquist plots at 1.53 V vs. RHE show a-RNMO charge transfer resistance Rct = 15.33 ± 0.36 Ω, lowest among samples.
nodes.evidence_snippet: EIS Nyquist plots were measured under identical condition (η = 300 mV). Using the equivalent-circuit model (inset of Fig. 3c) for fitting, a-RNMO showed the smallest Nyquist semicircle and the lowest charge-transfer resistance (Rct) (Supplementary Table 3)... The charge transfer resistances (Rct) of a-RNMO, a-NMO, c-NMO, and RuO2 were 15.33 ± 0.36 Ω, 48.82 ± 0.76 Ω, 890.70 ± 9.86 Ω, and 101.80 ± 1.18 Ω, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: BET surface area used for normalizing OER currents to specific activity.
nodes.evidence_snippet: To minimize the effect of morphology, the OER currents were normalized to the specific Brunauer–Emmett–Teller (BET) surface area (Supplementary Fig. 16).

nodes.characterization_summary: CV measured double-layer capacitance Cdl to estimate ECSA; a-RNMO showed highest specific activity 0.95 mA cm⁻² ECSA.
nodes.evidence_snippet: To evaluate the true catalytic activity of electrocatalysts, the electrochemically active surface area (ECSA) was estimated from double‑layer capacitance (Cdl) measurements (Supplementary Fig. 17).

nodes.characterization_summary: Ex-situ ICP-MS after OER shows negligible Ru and Ni dissolution (<0.25 ppm) within 100 hours, while Mo loss >10x higher.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Ex-situ ICP-MS test was supplemented. As shown in Supplementary Fig. 25 and Table 6, the dissolution of Ru and Ni was negligible within 100 hours (below 0.25 ppm), while Mo loss was more than ten times to those of Ru and Ni.

nodes.characterization_summary: In-situ Raman shows Mo-O feature (~900 cm⁻¹) disappears in a-RNMO above 1.30 V indicating rapid Mo dissolution; NiOOH peaks at 470 cm⁻¹ and 555 cm⁻¹ appear above 1.25 V.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In-situ Raman spectroscopy (Supplementary Fig. 26 and 27) was used to detect the intermediate states of the catalyst... The Mo–O feature at near 900 cm⁻¹, disappeared in a-RNMO above 1.30 V, suggesting a rapid Mo dissolution... Moreover, when the applied potential was above 1.25 V, a-RNMO displayed peaks at 470 cm⁻¹ and 555 cm⁻¹, attributing to the bending vibrational mode of Eg (δ(Ni3+-O)) and the stretching vibrational mode of A1g (ν(Ni3+-O)) in NiOOH.
